posts.excerpt: With Skype under Microsoft ownership, Rebtel now claims to be the largest independent mobile VoIP provider, with 17 million users in over 200 countries accessing its service over WiFi and 3G on iPhone, Android, and PCs. Rebtel has added two million users since February, and is seeing an average of 650K new users a month — many of whom have been attracted by its low-cost calling to landlines and mobile, along with the ability to switch between data and voice connections to avoid dropped calls and busy networks.

posts.title: Nordic start-ups follow Skype with low-cost calls
posts.author: Tarmo Virki
posts.excerpt: Europe's traditional phone companies, already under pressure from cheap internet-based services like Skype, are about to face more competition from a group of Nordic start-ups that will offer low-cost mobile calls and other services.

posts.title: Openet Raises $21 Million in Series D Funding
posts.author: Andrea Kavanagh
posts.excerpt: Openet, a global leader of high performance transaction management software for network operators today announced it has completed a $21 million funding round (€16.9 million). The investment will enable Openet to serve accelerating customer demand by financing the development of direct and indirect distribution channels, product development, product management and deployment engineering.

posts.title: MedicAnimal Ltd acquires Petmeds.co.uk
posts.author: Carmen Murray
posts.excerpt: 19 August 2012, London – MedicAnimal Ltd, the UK’s largest online retailer of pet food and healthcare supplies has agreed to acquire Petmeds.co.uk, an online store for animal medicines, food and grooming products.

posts.title: We're Hiring
posts.author: Rob Moffat
posts.excerpt: Balderton Capital are seeking a bright, motivated invidual for the role of VC Associate. Please send all applications to Rob Moffat (rmoffat@balderton.com).

posts.title: Housetrip secures $40m Series C from Accel, Balderton & Index
posts.author: Ryan Levitt
posts.excerpt: LONDON – 9 October 2012 – HouseTrip.com, one of the largest holiday rental websites in the world, today announces a USD$40M Series C funding round led by Accel Partners, with existing investors Balderton Capital and Index Ventures also participating.

posts.title: Getting Into Bed with Venture Capital
posts.author: Amy Wilson
posts.excerpt: Joe Murray and Richard Tucker have rescued thousands of sofas, beds and mattresses from a life languishing in Britain's warehouses. It's not a mission of mercy, it's a key part of the strategy of WorldStores, the online furniture and homewares business they founded in 2007.

posts.title: Tictail raises seed round from Balderton Capital and Klaus Hommels
posts.author: Jennie Wachtmeister
posts.excerpt: London, 22 October 2012: Tictail, the DIY ecommerce platform from Sweden voted one of the top 100 startups by Wired, has raised €1.2 million in seed funding in a round led by Balderton Capital and Klaus Hommels, it was announced today.

posts.title: SAATCHI ONLINE LAUNCHES ORIGINAL HOLIDAY COLLECTION FOR ART LOVERS
posts.author: Nicole Garton
posts.excerpt: Los Angeles – October 24, 2012 (5:05am PST): Saatchi Online is offering a unique holiday collection titled 12XTwelve, which features 65 new works of art from its worldwide community of emerging artists. Rebecca Wilson, Director of the Saatchi Gallery London and Head of Artist Relations, Saatchi Online, has invited a select group of artists to create one-of-a-kind art exclusively for the 12XTwelve project.

posts.title: "We Back People Who Want to Be Rich Not Famous"
posts.author: Bobbie Johnson
posts.excerpt: For one of Europe’s most influential investors, Barry Maloney keeps a low profile. The big, genial Irishman is the driving force behind Balderton Capital — the London-based VC with one of the best hit rates around. But he doesn't often give interviews. “We prefer to let our companies do the talking,” he says, when we meet for coffee at the company’s offices right in the center of the British capital.

posts.title: Are We Ready To Archive Our Online Lives?
posts.author: David Meyer
posts.excerpt: Archify isn’t the first service to promise a personal search engine but, with smart touches such as Gmail integration and the recording of social streams, it has a decent chance of being the one that succeeds.

posts.title: QUBIT ANNOUNCES $7.5 MILLION SERIES A INVESTMENT LED BY BALDERTON CAPITAL
posts.author: Patrick Herridge
posts.excerpt: LONDON – 4th December 2012 - QuBit (www.qubitproducts.com), the customer data platform, has today closed a $7.5 million Series A funding round led by the EU’s leading venture investor, Balderton Capital (www.balderton.com). Bernard Liautaud, General Partner at Balderton Capital and previously founder of Business Objects, will also be joining QuBit’s board.

posts.title: Intune Networks delivers world's first NEBS certified distributed switch
posts.author: Richard Brandon
posts.excerpt: The iVX8000, Intune's unique packet optical switching system, becomes the world's first distributed switch to be NEBS certified for use in carrier networks in the United States.

posts.title: Balderton Invests In Rentify
posts.author: Daniel Smith
posts.excerpt: London, January 11th 2013 Rentify, the UK's leading software platform for landlords, has secured a £2 million Series A investment from Balderton Capital, the leading venture capital investor in Europe.

posts.title: Kobalt Launches Label Services Division, Preps New Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds Release
posts.author: Andrew Hampp
posts.excerpt: Not only did Kobalt sign a deal with Dave Grohl this week, the company is also formally introducing a new Label Services division that will handle digital and physical releases for independent artists as well as Kobalt clients. Though the division has quietly released several albums in recent months, most notably gospel act Larry Callahan & Selected of God's "The Evolution II," it will gain major attention next month with the release of Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds' "Push the Sky Away," due out Feb. 18 through Kobalt Label Services (KLS) and Cave's Bad Seed Ltd.

posts.title: The Hut Buys Cycling Retailer Probikekit.com
posts.author: Graham Ruddick
posts.excerpt: The cycling retail boom driven by the success of the London 2012 Olympics has continued after The Hut Group, which is backed by Sir Stuart Rose and Sir Terry Leahy, acquired accessories business probikekit.com.

posts.title: Shining a Spotlight on Venture Capital
posts.author: BEN ROONEY
posts.excerpt: European tech entrepreneurs often look enviously at their U.S. counterparts when it comes to their venture capital backers. European VCs are parsimonious and risk-averse, they complain, compared with the deals of their U.S. counterparts.

posts.title: 5 Consumer-Driven Technologies That Will Reshape Society
posts.author: SETH PRIEBATSCH
posts.excerpt: Technology consumers, not companies, are driving nothing less than revolutions based on demand for alternatives to expensive dinosaur institutions. Seth Priebatsch of LevelUp predicts which will be the next titans to fall.

posts.title: Casual-game Developer Big Fish Celebrates 10 Years and 2 Billion Downloads
posts.author: Jeffrey Grubb
posts.excerpt: Casual-game developer Big Fish recorded its most successful year on record in 2012. The company generated over $220 million in revenue for the year and reached two billion total game downloads since it started in 2002. ﻿

posts.title: Intune Networks Wins Red Herring Top 100 Europe Award
posts.author: Richard Brandon
posts.excerpt: Intune is chosen ahead of hundreds of other technology companies for this prestigious award. Red Herring announced its Top 100 award winners today, recognizing Europe’s leading private companies and celebrating these startups’ innovations and technologies across their respective industries.

posts.title: Quickly does it
posts.author: C.S.W.
posts.excerpt: FOR many shop owners, e-commerce remains a riddle. Each step, from creating an online shopfront that lures in customers to taking payment for goods, can flummox retailers selling their wares online. In many cases, intimate knowledge of such technical wizardry as Perl, PHP and MySQL databases is needed.
